I. GENERAL
Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are becoming more diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community, and public spheres.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that is less supportive in reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, erroneous interpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly in terms of prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

Article 21
In carrying out the duties as referred to in Article 20, UPPTK has the following obligations:
1. to coordinate and consult with PPT PKBGA;
2. to document and report every case of gender-based violence and violence against children that it handles to PPT PKBGA.

This is prevention through education/IEC activities. The retrieved English passage correctly captures this, and the judge’s rationale is consistent with the source. 6.5.rationale: The Indonesian regulation does not set out disability-specific services, but it does include disability/impairment as a protected characteristic under the non-discrimination principle. In the official elucidation of Pasal 2 huruf a, it states protection is provided “tanpa membedakan ... kondisi fisik maupun mental.” This directly covers people with physical or mental conditions (a common legal phrasing encompassing disability). The retrieved candidates included this exact language (English: “physical or mental condition”), so a judge applying an indicator that only asks whether disability is recognized/included should answer Yes. The judge appears to have applied an overly strict standard (requiring special targeted measures), leading to a false negative despite available evidence.

Letter a What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter b What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
Letter c What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.
What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, compatible, and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.
Letter d What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Letter e What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.
What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to be creative and to engage in recreation.
Letter f What is meant by the principle of "respect for the child's opinion" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter g What is meant by the principle of "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.
Letter h What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.
Letter i What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.
Letter j What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Purbalingga Regency.
Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
Sub-district is a part of the Regency Region led by a Sub-district Head.
Sub-district Head is the leader of the Sub-district who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which are and are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
Victims of Gender-Based Violence are people who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
Child Victims of Violence are children who receive harsh treatment both physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of strengthening victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with determined operational standards.
Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unified implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
Complaint Service Unit at Sub-district Level hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the sub-district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 23
In implementing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may conduct cooperation with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.
Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.
The implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURBALINGGA REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF
GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND VIOLENCE AGAINST CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are becoming more diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community, and public spheres.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that is less supportive in reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, erroneous interpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly in terms of prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

REGENT OF PURBALINGGA
CENTRAL JAVA PROVINCE
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURBALINGGA REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN
BY THE GRACE OF GOD ALMIGHTY
THE REGENT OF PURBALINGGA,

Considering : that every person has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security, free from all forms of acts of violence, discrimination and human rights violations;

that the number of victims of gender-based violence and children has increased so that victims must receive protection from violence and/or threats of violence both inside and outside the household;

that victims of violence need to have their dignity and honor protected and their right to life guaranteed without discrimination and to provide legal certainty;

that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children;

In View of :

CHAPTER IV
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION
Part One
General

CHAPTER VII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 28
The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance and supervision over the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and child victims.
The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the Regional Apparatus.

CHAPTER IX
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 30
At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and child victims are declared to remain in effect as long as they have not been replaced and do not conflict with the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

CHAPTER V
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Article 24
The implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and child victims is a joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. local government;
b. society;
c. family; and
d. parents.

REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES
PURBALINGGA REGENCY
REGENT OF PURBALINGGA
DECIDES:
To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILD VICTIMS.

CHAPTER VIII
FUNDING
Article 29
All activities related to the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget and/or from other legitimate and non-binding receipts.

Article 10
Prevention Efforts as referred to in Article 9 letter a include:
1. conducting communication, information, and education about gender-based and child violence;
2. disseminating laws and regulations related to gender-based and child violence.

Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, is carried out by: PPT PKBGA; and

Article 21
In carrying out the duties as referred to in Article 20, UPPTK has the following obligations:
1. to coordinate and consult with PPT PKBGA;
2. to document and report every case of gender-based violence and violence against children that it handles to PPT PKBGA.

6.7.rationale: The Indonesian text explicitly includes minority-related grounds in its non-discrimination principle. In the elucidation of Pasal 2 huruf a, protection is provided “tanpa membedakan suku, agama, ras, golongan, ... etnis, budaya, bahasa, status hukum ...”. These terms (suku/etnis/agama/ras/budaya/bahasa) cover minority groups. The retrieved candidates contained this language, but the judge required “special/targeted protection measures” for minority women rather than recognizing that the policy affirmatively commits to non-discrimination across minority characteristics. This is a reasoning/threshold error given the evidence shown.
